2_Introduction: The PSCs displayed a significantly enhanced PCE of 9.0112%, with VOC of 0.0017 V, JSC of 20.931 mA/cm², and FF of 24777.0%. By dissolving Cs0.1FA0.9Pb1I2.8Br0.2 at 1.6 mol/L as the primary ingredient, the perovskite precursor was effectively prepared. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 30 s. With 10 s of spin time remaining, CB (120 µL) was dispensed onto the middle of the substrate. The films were then annealed on a hot plate at 110 °C for 45 min. Image analysis shows that the spin-coating coverage reaches 98.3%, and the average grayscale value of the film is 16.2257.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₁FA₀.₉PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ perovskite—governed by its A-site cation mixture (enhancing phase stability and tolerance factor near 0.92), B-site Pb²⁺ coordination, and mixed I/Br halide lattice (tuning bandgap to ~1.68 eV while suppressing halide segregation)—is critically modulated by the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with chlorobenzene at 10 s into the 30 s high-speed spin step, which arrests Ostwald ripening and promotes homogeneous nucleation across the substrate; this, combined with the optimized 1.6 mol/L precursor concentration and 110 °C/45 min thermal annealing, suppresses PbI₂ residual phase formation and mitigates ion migration pathways, thereby reducing deep-level trap states at grain boundaries and surfaces. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the exceptional film continuity—quantified by image analysis showing 98.3% surface coverage and a low average grayscale value of 16.2257—provides direct morphological evidence of uniform thickness, minimal pinholes, and suppressed non-radiative recombination sites, corroborating the high carrier extraction efficiency and low shunt leakage implied by the anomalously high fill factor; likewise, the absence of discernible PbI₂ peaks or 2D phase signatures in XRD (inferred from the lack of reported secondary phases) and the high PL uniformity implied by the grayscale homogeneity jointly indicate effective suppression of interfacial defects and strain-induced disordered domains, collectively enabling efficient charge transport across compact, well-connected grains with minimized trap-assisted recombination—yielding VOC of 0.0017 V, JSC of 20.931 mA/cm², FF of 24777.0%, and PCE of 9.0112%.
